title: In excelsis Gloria.
meterSource: The book does not print a numerical meter. Each pair of two-pulse printed spans has been represented as one 4/4 measure for the app.

measures.notesAboutNotation: A printed double bar precedes the repeated In excelsis Gloria text; forte marking appears above the entry.

notationConventions.raw: Colon (:) separates rhythmic pulse cells; | separates the two printed halves of a combined 4/4 measure. The scan often has one barline per two-pulse span.
notationConventions.rhythm: Period (.) and comma (,) inside a cell subdivide its pulse. -r prolongs the previous note for half a pulse and attacks r for the second half. '—' means continuation.
notationConventions.accidentals: fi, si and ta are chromatic tonic-solfa syllables, not text typos.

issues: The printed page does not specify numeric meter or tempo. 4/4 is an editorial grouping of paired two-pulse spans; 90 BPM is a UI fallback.
A few unclear lower-octave and chromatic syllables should be checked visually before treating playback as definitive.
The printed underline groupings are only partially encoded by underlineBeats. Raw notation preserves textual grouping.
The printed double bar before the second In excelsis refrain has been annotated; it is not interpreted as a playback repeat instruction.
The last printed colon and fermata imply a final sustained cadence; the exact performance-length of the fermata is not specified.
MIDI register is a practical SATB allocation, not an independently verified voice register.
